checked: The summary describes the actual scope; sentence openings vary and none of the listed stock AI phrases occurs.

General Information uses the permitted three-section layout. No computational formula is used in any example. The one-third House and two-thirds Senate thresholds are first taught in Core Concept, House Charge and Senate Trial.

Examples cover included President, excluded lower judge, unlisted ground, six substantive grounds, regular and direct filing, Senate conviction threshold, and Ombudsman delay remedy. The cases progress from list recognition to procedural application; no case is merely a noun or number replacement.
Every multi-step solution is a numbered list with no unnumbered instruction before it. No key numerical computation requires a display equation.

L21.note: There are no display equations in this constitutional lesson.

checked: Body paragraphs contain at most three sentences. The sole bullet list groups the impeachable offices.

L23.note: No illustration placeholders or figure-dependent questions occur.

checked: Impeachment and conviction are defined before the grounds; each of the six grounds is explained before its example. Verified complaint, articles, and censure are glossed before application. Thresholds identify their denominators as all House Members or all Senators.

Public trust is explained as answering to people and serving honestly. Each ground has meaning or conduct, House and Senate roles explain the process, and Ombudsman investigation and corrective directions explain remedies.

Ground matching is expressly separated from proof; deliberate breach is contrasted with mistake; treason requires war; other high crimes excludes automatic treatment of minor offenses. Filing routes, all-member thresholds, one-year bar, and separate criminal punishment state limits.
